question: A 45-year-old man comes to the physician for a follow-up examination after being diagnosed with hypertension 6 months ago. He has cut salt out of his diet and started exercising regularly, but home blood pressure measurements continue to be elevated. His blood pressure is 160/85 mm Hg. An antihypertensive medication is prescribed that decreases blood pressure by decreasing the transmembrane calcium current across vascular smooth muscle cells. Side effects include peripheral edema and flushing. Which of the following best describes why this drug does not affect skeletal muscle contraction?

options.opa: Skeletal muscle lacks voltage-gated L-type calcium channels
options.opb: Skeletal muscle contraction occurs independently of extracellular calcium influx
options.opc: Skeletal muscle ryanodine receptor activation occurs independently of membrane depolarization
options.opd: Skeletal muscle preferentially expresses N-type and P-type calcium channels
options.ope: Skeletal muscle calcium channels do not undergo conformational change when bound to this drug

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Antihypertensive medication decreases transmembrane calcium current" -> "Vascular smooth muscle relaxation occurs" -> "Blood pressure decreases" -> "Skeletal muscle contraction is not affected" -> "Skeletal muscle lacks voltage-gated L-type calcium channels" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Antihypertensive medication targets calcium channels" -> "Calcium influx in vascular smooth muscle is reduced" -> "Vasodilation occurs" -> "Skeletal muscle contraction remains unchanged" -> "Skeletal muscle contraction occurs independently of extracellular calcium influx" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle are affected by the drug" -> "Calcium influx is decreased" -> "Vascular smooth muscle relaxes" -> "Skeletal muscle contraction is not influenced" -> "Skeletal muscle ryanodine receptor activation occurs independently of membrane depolarization" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Drug decreases calcium current in vascular smooth muscle" -> "Blood pressure lowers" -> "Skeletal muscle contraction is unaffected" -> "Skeletal muscle preferentially expresses N-type and P-type calcium channels" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Medication reduces calcium influx in vascular smooth muscle" -> "Vasodilation leads to lower blood pressure" -> "Skeletal muscle contraction remains intact" -> "Skeletal muscle calcium channels do not undergo conformational change when bound to this drug" -> 75%
analysis: Skeletal muscle contraction primarily relies on the release of calcium from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, which is triggered by the activation of ryanodine receptors. This process is largely independent of extracellular calcium influx, which is the mechanism affected by the drug described. Therefore, the correct explanation for why this drug does not affect skeletal muscle contraction is that skeletal muscle contraction occurs independently of extracellular calcium influx.
